laws.name: American Privacy Rights Act
laws.threshold: As proposed: most businesses under FTC jurisdiction, with a small-business exemption.
laws.summary: The most-watched federal proposal. Would set national data minimization rules and preempt most state privacy laws.
laws.build:
- Nothing here is required today
- Collect only the data each feature needs; data minimization is the core of every federal proposal and already law in Maryland

laws.name: California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the CPRA
laws.enforcer: California Privacy Protection Agency and Attorney General
laws.threshold: For-profit businesses doing business in California with $25M+ annual revenue (inflation-adjusted), OR that buy, sell, or share data of 100K+ California consumers or households, OR that earn 50%+ of revenue from selling or sharing personal data.
laws.summary: California's privacy law, expanded by the CPRA. Covers sharing for cross-context advertising, not just sales. The CPPA's 2026 regulations add risk assessments, cybersecurity audits for larger businesses, and rules for automated decision-making technology (ADMT compliance from January 1, 2027). Limited private right of action for data breaches.
laws.build:
- "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" link in the footer (or one combined opt-out link)
- "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information" link if you use sensitive data beyond what's needed to provide the service
- Treat Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signals as a valid opt-out, with no extra steps
- Notice at collection shown at or before the point data is collected (sign-up forms, SDKs, apps)
- Privacy policy updated at least every 12 months, including retention periods per data category
- At least two ways to submit requests; confirm receipt within 10 business days, respond within 45 days, process opt-outs within 15 business days
- Access, deletion, correction, and portability workflows with identity verification
- No dark patterns: opting out can't take more steps than opting in
- Data minimization: collect only what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes
- Risk assessments before high-risk processing; ADMT notice and opt-out for significant decisions from January 1, 2027
- CCPA-compliant contracts with service providers, contractors, and third parties
- No penalty or degraded service for exercising rights (financial incentives need a notice)
laws.next: January 1, 2027: ADMT notice, opt-out, and access rules apply.

laws.name: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act
laws.threshold: As proposed: services directed to, or knowingly used by, minors under 17.
laws.summary: Would extend COPPA to teens, ban targeted ads to minors, and add an eraser button. Several states already restrict ads and data sales for known minors.
laws.build:
- Nothing here is required today
- Build age signals so you can identify users under 17
- Architect ad systems so targeted ads can be switched off for minors
- Build an 'eraser button' so parents and teens can delete teen data

laws.name: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act
laws.threshold: Operators of websites and online services directed to children under 13, or with actual knowledge they collect data from children under 13.
laws.summary: Requires verifiable parental consent before collecting children's data. The FTC's amended rule, enforceable April 22, 2026, adds separate consent for third-party disclosure, a written retention policy, and a written security program.
laws.build:
- Neutral age screen that doesn't nudge kids to lie about their age
- Verifiable parental consent before collecting any personal information from children under 13
- Separate parental consent before disclosing children's data to third parties such as advertisers
- Direct notice to parents and an online privacy notice describing data practices
- Parent dashboard or process to review, delete, and revoke consent for their child's data
- Written data retention policy; delete children's data once it's no longer needed
- Written children's information security program
- Don't require more data than reasonably necessary for a child to participate

laws.name: Colorado Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Colorado consumers per year, or 25K+ consumers and earning any revenue (or discounts) from selling personal data. Biometric rules apply regardless of size.
laws.summary: Detailed AG regulations govern notices, consent, and assessments. Universal opt-out signals required since July 2024. 2024 amendments added protections for known minors (Oct 2025) and biometric data (July 2025). Cure period has ended.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice meeting Colorado's rule-specified content requirements
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day response clock and appeal process
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals such as GPC
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data, refreshed at the intervals the Colorado rules set
- No dark patterns in consent flows
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing, kept on file
- Known minors under 18: consent before targeted ads, sale, or profiling, and assess heightened risk of harm
- Biometric data: written retention and deletion policy and consent, regardless of the user-count threshold
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Connecticut Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Since July 1, 2026: controllers that process data of 35K+ Connecticut consumers, OR process any sensitive data, OR offer any personal data for sale.
laws.summary: Now one of the broadest state laws: any sale or sensitive-data processing triggers coverage. Adds profiling contest rights, LLM-training disclosure, and new sensitive categories. Selling precise geolocation is banned from October 1, 2026.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice stating whether personal data is used to train large language models, request methods, and month/year last updated
- Request flow for access (including inferences), correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- List of third parties that bought a consumer's data, available on request
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling; honor GPC and other universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data, which now includes neural data, financial account credentials, and government ID numbers
- Profiling decisions with legal or similar effects: explain the reason, let users review data and contest the result, and run an impact assessment
- Do not sell precise geolocation data
- Never return SSNs, account numbers, or similar identifiers in access responses
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Delaware Personal Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 35K+ Delaware consumers, or 10K+ consumers and earning over 20% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: Low thresholds. Consumers can get a list of specific third parties. Consent required to sell data of, or target ads to, known teens 13-17.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- List of specific third parties that received a consumer's data, available on request
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data
- Consent before selling or targeting ads to consumers you know are 13-17
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Schools receiving federal education funding. Ed-tech vendors are bound through school contracts under the 'school official' exception.
laws.summary: Controls disclosure of student education records. Vendors may use records only as the school directs. Many states add stricter student privacy laws.
laws.build:
- Use student records only for the purpose the school authorized
- No re-disclosure of student records to other parties without school authorization
- No advertising or profiling using student education records
- Let the school control the data: support access, amendment, and deletion requests routed through the school
- Delete or return student data at contract end
- Check state student privacy laws too (California SOPIPA and similar)

laws.name: General Data Protection Regulation
laws.threshold: Any organization offering goods or services to, or monitoring the behavior of, people in the EU, wherever the organization is based.
laws.summary: The global benchmark. Lawful basis for every use of data, strict consent for cookies, 72-hour breach notice, and fines up to 4% of global revenue.
laws.build:
- Document a lawful basis (consent, contract, legitimate interests, etc.) for each processing purpose before launch
- Cookie consent banner: no non-essential cookies or trackers until the user opts in, with reject as easy as accept
- Privacy notice meeting Articles 13-14
- Request flow for access, deletion, correction, portability, restriction, and objection, answered within one month
- Records of processing activities (Article 30)
- DPIA before high-risk processing
- Data processing agreements with every vendor; Standard Contractual Clauses or EU-US Data Privacy Framework for US transfers
- Process to notify the regulator of a breach within 72 hours
- Privacy by design and default
- EU representative if you have no EU establishment; DPO if required

laws.name: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
laws.threshold: Financial institutions significantly engaged in financial activities, including many fintechs, lenders, and payment companies.
laws.summary: Privacy notices, opt-out of sharing with non-affiliates, and the Safeguards Rule's security program requirements. Several states (CA, CT, MN, MT, OR) no longer exempt financial companies at the entity level.
laws.build:
- Initial privacy notice at account opening, and annual notices unless you qualify for the exception
- Opt-out before sharing customer data with nonaffiliated third parties (with listed exceptions)
- Safeguards Rule: written information security program run by a named qualified individual
- Encryption of customer information in transit and at rest, and MFA for anyone accessing it
- Written risk assessment, regular testing, and vendor oversight
- Notify the FTC within 30 days of discovering a breach affecting 500 or more consumers
- Identity checks so callers can't social-engineer account data

laws.name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
laws.threshold: Health plans, health care providers, and clearinghouses, and the business associates that handle PHI for them.
laws.summary: Privacy, Security, and Breach Notification Rules for protected health information. Health apps outside HIPAA are still covered by state sensitive-data rules and the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule.
laws.build:
- Signed Business Associate Agreement with every vendor that touches PHI (cloud hosting, analytics, support tools, AI vendors)
- Access controls, unique user IDs, audit logs, and encryption for electronic PHI
- Use and show only the minimum necessary PHI for each function
- Patient access requests fulfilled within 30 days
- Do not send PHI to advertising or analytics pixels and SDKs without a BAA
- Written risk analysis and risk management plan under the Security Rule
- Breach notification to individuals within 60 days of discovery

laws.name: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Any private entity that collects biometric identifiers (face geometry, fingerprints, voiceprints, iris or hand scans) from Illinois residents. No size threshold.
laws.summary: The most litigated privacy law in the U.S. Anyone can sue for $1,000 per negligent violation or $5,000 per reckless one, without proving harm. The 2024 amendment limited damages to one recovery per person.
laws.build:
- Applies to face-based photo tagging, voice login, ID verification, and similar features
- Public written policy with a retention schedule and destruction rules
- Written notice of what is collected, why, and for how long, then a signed written release (electronic signature counts) before collecting
- Never sell, lease, trade, or profit from biometric data
- No disclosure to vendors without consent
- Destroy biometric data when the purpose is met or within 3 years of the user's last interaction, whichever comes first
- Store and protect it at least as well as other confidential data

laws.name: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Indiana consumers, or 25K+ consumers and earning over 50% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: New in 2026. Closely follows Virginia. Permanent 30-day cure period.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability, with identity verification and a 45-day response clock
- Appeal process for denied requests
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling
- Opt-in consent screen before collecting sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before launching targeted ads, data sales, profiling, or sensitive-data features
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Iowa Consumer Data Protection Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Iowa consumers per year, or 25K+ consumers and earning over 50% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: A narrow law: no correction right, no targeted-ad opt-out, no assessments. Longest response clock (90 days) and cure period (90 days).
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, deletion, and portability with a 90-day response clock and appeal process
- Opt-out of sale
- Clear notice and an opt-out before processing sensitive data
- Reasonable data security
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Kentucky consumers, or 25K+ consumers and earning over 50% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: New in 2026. Closely follows Virginia. 30-day cure period.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability, with identity verification and a 45-day response clock
- Appeal process for denied requests
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling
- Consent screen before collecting sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before launching targeted ads, data sales, profiling, or sensitive-data features
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Maryland Online Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 35K+ Maryland consumers, or 10K+ consumers and earning over 20% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: The strictest state law. Data minimization is a hard limit, sensitive data can be processed only when strictly necessary, and selling sensitive data is banned outright.
laws.build:
- Collect only data that is reasonably necessary and proportionate to the service the user asked for; this is a hard limit, not a disclosure
- Sensitive data: collect or process only when strictly necessary to provide the requested service; consent does not cure it
- Never sell sensitive data
- No sale or targeted advertising to users you know, or should have known, are under 18
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- Data protection assessment for each algorithm used in high-risk processing
- Audit existing data flows against the necessity standard

laws.name: Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Minnesota consumers, or 25K+ consumers and earning over 25% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: Adds a right to question profiling decisions and requires a written data inventory. Must explain the reason when denying a request.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock; explain the reason when denying a request
- List of specific third parties that received a consumer's data, available on request
- Right to question profiling results: tell users the reason for a significant decision and let them review data and request re-evaluation
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data; no sale or targeted ads to known users under 16 without consent
- Written data inventory and documented privacy and security policies
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Since October 1, 2025: controllers processing data of 25K+ Montana consumers, or 15K+ consumers and earning over 25% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: SB 297 cut the threshold in half and eliminated the cure period, so the AG can act on a first violation. Requires a clearly labeled opt-out link.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice with the content required by the 2025 amendment, including a clearly labeled opt-out link
- Notify users of material privacy changes and let them withdraw earlier consent
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- Never return SSNs, account numbers, or similar identifiers in access responses
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing

laws.name: Nebraska Data Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Any business processing Nebraska residents' data that is not an SBA-defined small business. No user-count threshold.
laws.summary: Follows the Texas model. Permanent 30-day cure period. Product teams often miss it because there is no user-count threshold.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability, with identity verification and a 45-day response clock
- Appeal process for denied requests
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling
- Opt-in consent screen before collecting sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before launching targeted ads, data sales, profiling, or sensitive-data features
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: New Hampshire Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 35K+ New Hampshire consumers, or 10K+ consumers and earning over 25% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: Modeled on Connecticut's original law. Universal opt-out signals honored. Cure period became discretionary in 2026.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data
- Consent before selling or targeting ads to consumers you know are 13-15
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: New Jersey Data Privacy Act
laws.enforcer: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ New Jersey consumers (excluding payment-only data), or 25K+ consumers and earning any revenue or discounts from selling data.
laws.summary: Any revenue from data sales triggers coverage at 25K consumers. Broad sensitive data definition includes financial information. Assessments must happen before high-risk processing starts.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data, which includes financial information and status as transgender or non-binary
- Consent before selling, targeting ads to, or profiling consumers you know are 13-17
- Data protection assessment before starting high-risk processing, not after
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Oregon consumers per year, or 25K+ consumers and earning 25%+ of revenue from selling data. Covers nonprofits.
laws.summary: Covers nonprofits since July 2025. Consumers can demand the specific third parties that got their data. Bans selling precise geolocation and data of known under-16s from January 2026. Cure period ended January 2026.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- List of the specific third parties that received a consumer's data, available on request
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data
- Do not sell precise geolocation data or the data of consumers you know are under 16
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Nonprofits are covered: don't assume an exemption
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 35K+ Rhode Island consumers (excluding payment-only data), or 10K+ consumers and earning over 20% of revenue from selling data. Every commercial website collecting Rhode Island customer data must post a privacy notice regardless of size.
laws.summary: New in 2026. Low thresholds and no cure period. The privacy notice must name the third parties you sell data to.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories collected and every third party you sell to or may sell to (required for all commercial websites, even below the thresholds)
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability, with identity verification and a 45-day response clock
- Appeal process for denied requests
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling
- Opt-in consent screen before collecting sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you
- No cure period: ship compliant, there is no warning letter

checker.dutyBelow: Every commercial website collecting Rhode Island customer data must post a privacy notice, even below the thresholds.

laws.name: Tennessee Information Protection Act
laws.threshold: Requires $25M+ revenue AND either 175K+ Tennessee consumers or 25K+ consumers with over 50% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: High thresholds limit it to larger companies. A privacy program aligned to the NIST Privacy Framework is an affirmative defense. Penalties up to $15,000 per violation.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day clock and appeal process
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling
- Opt-in consent for sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Written privacy program aligned to the NIST Privacy Framework (gives you an affirmative defense)
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
laws.threshold: Any business processing Texas residents' data that is not an SBA-defined small business. No user-count threshold. Small businesses still need consent to sell sensitive data.
laws.summary: No volume threshold, so it reaches far more companies than most state laws. Universal opt-out signals required since January 2025. Texas has an active AG enforcement program.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- If you sell sensitive data, the exact notice text: "NOTICE: We may sell your sensitive personal data." (Biometric sales need their own version)
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability with a 45-day response clock and appeal process
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and profiling; honor universal opt-out signals
- Opt-in consent before processing sensitive data; even SBA small businesses must get consent before selling sensitive data
- Data protection assessment before high-risk processing
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Utah Consumer Privacy Act
laws.enforcer: Utah Attorney General and Division of Consumer Protection
laws.threshold: Requires BOTH $25M+ annual revenue AND either 100K+ Utah consumers or 25K+ consumers with over 50% of revenue from selling data.
laws.summary: The most business-friendly state law. No correction right, no assessments, and sensitive data needs only notice and an opt-out.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, deletion, and portability with a 45-day response clock
- Opt-out controls for sale and targeted advertising
- Clear notice and an opt-out before processing sensitive data
- Reasonable data security
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you

laws.name: Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act
laws.threshold: Controllers processing data of 100K+ Virginia consumers per year, or 25K+ consumers and earning over 50% of revenue from selling personal data.
laws.summary: The template most later state laws copied. Opt-in for sensitive data, data protection assessments, 30-day cure period, up to $7,500 per violation.
laws.build:
- Privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, third parties, and how to exercise rights
- Request flow for access, correction, deletion, and portability, with identity verification and a 45-day response clock
- Appeal process for denied requests, with a link to the AG complaint form
- Opt-out controls for sale, targeted advertising, and significant-decision profiling
- Opt-in consent screen before collecting sensitive data; parental consent for known children under 13
- Data protection assessment before launching targeted ads, data sales, profiling, or sensitive-data features
- Contracts with every vendor that processes personal data for you
